lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! We left Sunrise Harbor, and now we're in a new town. Listen. Can you hear it? It's so noisy! Welcome to the Bustling Market! There are fruit shops, fish shops and bread shops. Today's sentence is: There are many shops. Say it with me. There are many shops. Great! For one thing, say there is. There is a big fountain. For two or more, say there are. There are many shops. ひとつなら there is、ふたつ いじょうなら there are だよ。 Now, phonics. Look at these words. Boxes. Foxes. Buses. Glasses. When a word ends in x or s, we add e-s for two or more. Box, boxes. Bus, buses. Listen to the end. Iz, iz. x や s で おわる ことばは、es を つけて「イズ」と よむよ。 Here's a market tip. When you see something amazing, say, Wow, look at that! Let's say it. Wow, look at that! Okay, grab a basket and stay together. Let's go shopping!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're at a fruit shop. Look at all the fruit! Kiko wants peaches. How can she ask? Today's sentence is: Do you have any peaches? Say it with me. Do you have any peaches? Great! When you ask a question, use any. Do you have any cherries? The answer can be, Yes, we have some. Or, Sorry, we don't have any. しつもんと「ない」ときは any、「ある」ときは some だよ。 Let's practice. Do you have any pears? Yes, we have some! Now, phonics. Peach. Peaches. Lunch. Lunches. Sandwich. Sandwiches. Bench. Benches. Words that end in c-h also get e-s. And the end sounds like iz. ch で おわる ことばも es を つけて「イズ」。 Here's a shopping tip. When the shopkeeper says hello, say hello back and smile. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today is game day! The inn kitchen gave us a shopping list. We have two teams. Which team can finish first? Today's sentence is: We need some eggs and two apples. Say it with me. We need some eggs and two apples. Great! Need means we must have it. We can count eggs and apples, so we say two apples, three eggs. But milk and bread? Some milk. Some bread. かぞえられる ものは かずを、かぞえられない ものは some を つけるよ。 To ask, say, Do we have any milk? No, we don't. Now, let's review our phonics. Boxes. Peaches. Dishes. Tomatoes. Glasses. You can read them all! And when you write your list, don't forget the e-s. Here's a team tip. Read the list out loud together. Then nobody forgets anything. Ready, set, go! Let's go shopping, team!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Today we're writing recipe cards. With a recipe card, you can cook the same food again and again. A recipe card has two parts. First, what you need. You need ten strawberries and some cream. Second, the steps. Today's sentence is: Wash the strawberries. Cut them in half. Say it with me. Wash the strawberries. Cut them in half. Great! Them means the strawberries. In half means into two pieces. them は「それら」、in half は「はんぶんに」。 Then, put them on a plate with some cream. Three steps! Now, phonics review. Comb. Climb. Photo. Elephant. The b is quiet, and p-h says f. Super! Here's a writing tip. Start each step with an action word, and write a number for each step. One, two, three. Let's write our recipe cards!
